summary: This is a reference page for the Snowflake-style SQL command DROP PASSWORD POLICY, which removes a password policy from the system. It gives the syntax with an optional IF EXISTS clause, describes the name parameter's identifier rules, and lists the OWNERSHIP privilege required on the policy. The page also notes that operating on schema objects requires USAGE on the parent database and schema, and includes a usage query against policy_references and a single example dropping password_policy_production_1.
one_line: Reference for the DROP PASSWORD POLICY SQL command, covering syntax, identifier rules, required OWNERSHIP privilege, and an example.
key_facts: The DROP PASSWORD POLICY command removes a password policy from the system.
The syntax is DROP PASSWORD POLICY [ IF EXISTS ] <name>.
The name parameter is an identifier that must be unique for the account.
An identifier must start with an alphabetic character and cannot contain spaces or special characters unless enclosed in double quotes.
Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are case-sensitive.
The minimum privilege required is OWNERSHIP on the password policy.
OWNERSHIP is automatically granted to the role that created the object but can be transferred using the MANAGE GRANTS privilege.
Operating on any object in a schema also requires the USAGE privilege on the parent database and schema.
The usage note provides the query SELECT * from table(information_schema.policy_references(policy_name=>'<string>')) to check policy references.
The example drops a password policy named password_policy_production_1 with DROP PASSWORD POLICY password_policy_production_1;.
The page lists the policy-related sections Authentication Policy, Network Policy, Network Rule, Packages Policy, Session Policy and Secret as navigation links.
